penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Configuring retry/rollback policies for specific IoT platform architectures (hawkbit, AWS IoT, Azure IoT Hub) requires per-customer integration engineering that cannot be automated generically.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Selling to IoT platform engineering teams at industrial/automotive companies requires technical discovery, architecture review, and sales calls — no plausible self-serve path at the contract sizes needed.

rationale: IoT fleet operators genuinely suffer when transient OTA failures require manual recovery at scale, and companies deploying firmware to thousands of devices have budget to solve this. However, building a managed layer that sits above arbitrary device management platforms (hawkbit, AWS IoT, etc.) requires deep per-customer integration work — each customer's platform, device types, and failure semantics differ. Operational autonomy scores 3 because this is effectively a managed services play. Buildability with Claude/standard tooling scores 3 because it requires real infrastructure integration, not prompts and a Stripe link.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator with an AI factory. A managed retry/rollback layer for IoT OTA deployments requires integrating with each customer's specific device management platform via its API, understanding their device fleet topology, and configuring failure-handling logic — this is infrastructure engineering work. Even with Claude assisting, the operator would need to perform per-customer setup, monitor deployments, and support incidents. Reaching IoT engineering teams requires navigating long enterprise sales cycles. Drop this candidate unless a very specific, narrow wedge is identified (e.g. a one-click Stripe-purchased hawkbit plugin with fixed retry presets).
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (scored 3, need 7) and buildability_with_ai_min (scored 3, need 6). Infrastructure/integration-heavy play incompatible with autonomous factory model.
